item: the serving gate is a pure ASGI middleware that also refuses websockets, and never latches
summary: R644's gate was an @app.middleware("http"), which sees HTTP only, so a websocket route added later would have gone round it; and once open it latched. It is now a pure ASGI middleware: an HTTP request gets the fixed 503 and a websocket handshake is refused before it is accepted (uvicorn answers 403), and any other scope type but lifespan reaches nothing, until the startup checked the loop and armed airplane mode's guard, and the loop check, the serving loop and the armed guard are read on every request, so a guard uninstalled later, or a real socket call written back over a patched one, closes the gate again. Release line: the app's start-up safety gate now covers every kind of connection to it, not only page and API requests, and closes again if airplane mode's socket guard is ever taken away.
